question: Should OpenClaw expose opt-in reset-family transcript history through Gateway `chat.history` and model-facing `sessions_history`, while rejecting `includeFamily` with `offset`?
rationale: This changes a public/native/model-facing read contract and intentionally broadens authorized history retrieval to archived family transcripts; automation can verify implementation quality but cannot choose that product/security boundary.

options.title: Accept current opt-in contract
options.body: Land the PR after owner review, preserving the default active-only behavior, bounded/header-checked family reads, and explicit `includeFamily + offset` rejection.

options.title: Revise selector semantics
options.body: Ask the author to rename or narrow the selector, offset behavior, or archive inclusion rules before merge if maintainers want a different stable contract.

options.title: Keep archived family history out of core tools
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers decide archived transcript family recovery should stay in a different repair or administrative surface.

recommendation.title: Accept current opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Land the PR after owner review, preserving the default active-only behavior, bounded/header-checked family reads, and explicit `includeFamily + offset` rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent `sessions_history` pagination work touched the same Gateway/protocol/tool boundary and makes them the most specific available owner for this API decision.
